newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOK RECALL FOR WILLIAMS AFTER INJURY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOK RECALL FOR WILLIAMS AFTER INJURY.

text.p: Winger Chester Williams, one of South Africa's leading players in their 1995 World Cup triumph but out injured for all of last season, was included on Tuesday in the initial Springbok training squad preparing for the British Lions tour.
Williams, who scored four tries in South Africa's win over Western Samoa in the World Cup, was sidelined by a knee injury which required surgery.
Springbok manager Andre Markgraaff included Williams in a 27-man squad for a four-day programme at the Sports Science Institute in Cape Town.

"Due to certain circumstances we were not as well prepared as we could have been last year for the All Blacks tour," Markgraaff said. "This year we will be better prepared and we will be ready when the Lions arrive and for the Tri-Nations series.
"This testing programme is the first step in what we hope will be a highly successful season.".
The four-day programme will make use of state of the art equipment and test all areas of the player's physiological fitness levels.
South Africa lost four out of five tests against New Zealand in 1996, but were unbeaten on the close season tour of Argentina, France and Wales.

Markgraaf said that the 27 names should not be regarded as a guide to the composition of the Springboks. "There were at least another 13 or 14 that I wanted to include, but 27 was the maximum number who could be accomodated in the programme."

Squad: Andre Joubert, Jacques Olivier, James Small, Chester Williams, Andre Snymaan, Hennie le Roux, Japie Mulder, Henry Honiball, Joost van der Westhuizen, Johan Roux, Kevin Putt, Gary Teichmann, Ruben Kruger, Wayne Fyvie, Fritz van Heerden, Andre Veter, Hannes Strydom, Kobus Wiese, Mark Andrews, Johan Ackermann, Marius Hurter, Os du Randt, Dawie Theron, Toks van der Linde, Adrian Garvey, James Dalton, Henry Tromp.
